chunk_findings.detail:
`text.find("
" + head)` still selects the first line that begins with `# ddflow brief`, not necessarily the single H1 emitted by the view. Given a resume slice that itself contains a standalone `# ddflow brief` line before the real view heading -- for example `"## RESUME
# ddflow brief
recoverable work
# ddflow brief
## Work
"` -- the lead (`undecided`/reports/contest) is inserted after `## RESUME` and before the earlier slice line, so the new-work blocks still appear above recoverable work inside the RESUME section. The line anchor only excludes inline mentions and `##`/`###` headings; it does not verify the matched line is the view's actual heading, so B-brief-choices-above-resume can still occur.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py:_under_resume

chunk_findings.detail:
`_under_resume` still inserts at the first line-anchored `# ddflow brief`, not at the view heading. Given `text="## RESUME
# ddflow brief
old notes
# ddflow brief
## work
"` and a non-empty `undecided` (or any non-empty reports/contest lead), `text.find("
# ddflow brief")` hits the recovered H1 inside the RESUME slice and the lead is spliced there, so choices/reports land in the middle of recoverable work instead of immediately before the heading the view emits. The 54d60c06f probe only stops a non-line-start or `## ddflow brief` substring from matching; a prior brief quoted as its own H1 line still matches first. The `at < 0` branch also drops `lead` whenever the text neither contains `
# ddflow brief` nor starts with that exact heading, so reports, contest, and open-workflow choices vanish instead of being shown.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py:_under_resume
